title: Japan's Suica Penguin to Be Replaced by Rabbit
paragraphs: For 25 years, a penguin has been the face of Japan's Suica card, a prepaid card that people use to pay for train journeys and shopping.
But now, the penguin is getting ready to say goodbye.
JR East, the railway company behind Suica, has announced that a purple rabbit will replace the famous penguin in April 2027.
The company announced its new mascot in Tokyo on November 18.
The rabbit was chosen in a public vote. People could choose from three characters: a squirrel, a rabbit, and a third character carrying a small mole in a bag.
JR East chose the three characters from designs made by young artists. The company said it wanted a friendly new character that people could feel close to.
In total, around 1.6 million votes were cast, and the purple rabbit was the most popular choice, with about 860,000 votes.
But not everyone is happy about the change.
When JR East first announced that the penguin would be leaving, the news surprised many people.
And when the company showed the three possible new mascots in September, many people online said they didn't like the designs. Some felt that none of the new characters was as good as the penguin.
The penguin has been part of Suica since 2001, and its picture can be seen on the cards.
So even though the rabbit has won the public vote, winning the public's heart may take a little longer.
